newsitem.title: USA: DuPont employees given option to buy stock at $105.
newsitem.headline: DuPont employees given option to buy stock at $105.

text.p: DuPont Co. said Wednesday it will provide virtually all its employees an option to buy 100 shares of DuPont common stock at $105 per share as part of its DuPont Shares program.
The options can be exercised after the stock closing price is at least $150 on the New York Stock Exchange for five consecutive trading days. Options have a ten-year term.
The option price is based on the average of the high and low of DuPont stock on Jan. 29, which is the date the program was approved by the board of directors.
Participating employees, including those of DuPont's wholly owned energy subsidiary, Conoco, work in 70 countries on six continents.

For senior management, defined as vice presidents and above, the company said minimum stock ownership requirements and a modified stock option program will further align them with profitably growing the company and reflect a higher risk/reward component in their overall compensation. Stock ownership guidelines must be met within three years.
The company said it will purchase shares of its common stock to offset dilution resulting from shares issued under DuPont's compensation programs.

DuPont's board of directors has authorized the purchase and retirement of up to 10 million shares of common stock to offset dilution resulting from shares issued under DuPont's compensation programs. Shares will be purchased from time to time in the open market.
